afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 191109
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
409 AM MST Mon Oct 19 2026

.UPDATE...12Z Aviation Discussion

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A weak disturbance will spark scattered showers and isolated 
  thunderstorms this afternoon, mainly across the Arizona higher 
  terrain east of Phoenix.

- Temperatures during the next couple of days will warm to near to even
  a few degrees above normal before abrupt cooling takes place by
  the latter half of the week.

- A Pacific low pressure system moving into the region during the
  middle portion of the week will bringing heightened rain
  chances, mainly across south-central and eastern Arizona, with 
  the potential for multiple rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall 
  as well as some strong thunderstorms. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Tuesday/... 
Latest water vapor satellite imagery as well as objective analysis 
depict a weakening upper low over southwest AZ. This feature will 
move gradually move northeastward through central and northern 
portions of the state throughout the day. The associated ascent 
combined with sufficient moisture in the mid-levels will spark 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms this afternoon across 
portions of southeast AZ with some the activity making its way into 
the higher terrain areas of far eastern Maricopa and Pinal Counties 
and into southern Gila County. Due to more sun expected throughout 
the morning and early afternoon, diurnal heating will allow for some 
higher instability to materialize with the latest HREF showing 
MUCAPE values reaching upwards of 500 J/KG. Therefore, a few
stronger storms capable of producing gusty winds and brief heavy 
rainfall cannot be ruled out. As the upper-level low lifts 
northeastward and gets absorbed by the mean flow on Tuesday, 
rainfall chances will decrease across the region with any activity
limited across the White Mountains, where enough moisture 
combined with orographic lift will be sufficient to spark a few 
afternoon showers and storms. Otherwise, under the influence of 
more sun and slightly higher heights aloft in response to 
downstream ridging centered over northern Mexico, afternoon high 
temperatures today and Tuesday are expected to rebound to near 
normal levels as readings across most of the lower desert 
communities top out in the upper 80s with some of the normally 
warmer locations touching 90 degrees. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Wednesday through Sunday/... 
A much more active weather pattern is shaping up to take place by
the middle portion of the week as a deep upper-level low 
amplifies off the CA coast and then moves inland over the Desert 
Southwest through the remainder of the work week. Latest ensemble 
and deterministic model suite have come into a better agreement in
showing a deep upper-level low with strong negative height 
anomalies becoming established off the southern CA coast on 
Wednesday and potentially obtaining a slight negative tilt. This 
will cause the flow aloft to become established more out of the 
south, advecting deeper moisture northward into the region 
starting Tuesday night. In fact, both the EPS and GEFS show PWAT 
values peaking above 250% of normal with the North American 
Ensemble Forecasting System depicting moisture levels approaching 
near record values for mid-October. In addition, the combination 
of the deeper moisture as well as steeper mid-level lapse rates 
will likely lead to significant instability with both the ECMWF 
and GFS indicating MUCAPE values approaching 1000 J/KG. Therefore,
the combination of the strong synoptic ascent from the trough and
favorable thermodynamic parameters will likely lead to multiple 
rounds of showers and thunderstorms to break out across much of 
south-central AZ Wednesday through Thursday afternoon, period when
rainfall chances will be highest, while much of the western 
deserts should remain mostly dry given that the greatest moisture 
advection will occur mostly over central and eastern AZ. 

With the moderate levels of instability likely to be in place, any 
shower and thunderstorm activity will be capable of producing 
rainfall rates in excess of 1-2"/hr with training of activity likely 
to be an issue. Thus, there will be a heightened potential for flash 
flooding, especially across the foothills and higher terrain areas 
to the north and east of Phoenix where upslope flow will likely 
enhance the activity. Given this heightened potential for flash 
flooding, the Weather Prediction Center has placed areas from 
Phoenix and points north and east in a slight risk for excessive 
rainfall leading to flash flooding for both Wednesday and Thursday. 
In terms of rainfall amounts, the latest forecast from the Weather 
Prediction Center has much of the foothills and higher terrain areas 
north and east of Phoenix potentially receiving upwards of 1.00-
2.50" while across the lower deserts, including the Phoenix metro, 
amounts are likely to be lower ranging between 0.25-1.00", although 
locally higher amounts will be likely in areas that see training of 
activity. In addition to the heavy rainfall threat, given that the
0-6 km shear will be in excess of 50 kts combined with the 
moderate levels of instability, there will also be the threat of a
few strong to severe storms capable of producing strong wind 
gusts and hail. 

As the upper-level low moves inland into the southern Great Basin 
late Thursday, strong dry air advection will gradually push eastward 
ending rain chances by Thursday afternoon across the south-central 
AZ lower deserts with rain chances lingering into early Friday over 
the higher terrain. There are indications from guidance of a
follow-on shortwave moving through area late Friday through 
Saturday, however, it should be inconsequential given that there 
will be an abundance of dry air in place limiting any potential 
for additional rainfall.

Under the influence of the general troughing pattern as well as the 
heightened rain chances, temperatures by the latter half of the week 
will rapidly cool off towards readings that will be several degrees 
below normal. The latest NBM shows much of the lower deserts 
struggling to reach 80 degrees for afternoon highs both Thursday and 
Friday, with Friday likely to be coolest day. Temperatures will 
gradually warm up next weekend but still remain below normal. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1109Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No major aviation concerns are expected throughout the TAF period.
Winds will continue to be gennerally aob 5 kts which will promote
periods of VRB conditions throughout the period, and leaving
confidence low for an established westerly shift at KPHX this
afternoon. Winds will be returning back out of the east for the
overnight period for tueday, lasting well intot tuesday morning.
Chances for SHRA remain in the forecast but are expected to stay
far east from the terminals. FEW-SCT mid level clouds will persist
over the terminals, with the lowest bases around 7-10 kft.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No aviation concerns are expected over the next 24 hours under
mostly clear skies. KIPL will maintain a light W'rly flow before
going VRB tomorrow morning while, KBLH will maintain a light
NW'rly flow before also going VRB tomorrow morning. Wind speeds
will be light, aob 06kts, throughout the period. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Wind speeds through Tuesday will generally be light with limited
afternoon gustiness before increasing towards the middle of the
week ahead of an approaching weather system. Scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms are expected across the higher terrain
areas of the eastern districts this afternoon. Rainfall chances 
temporarily decrease on Tuesday before increasing substantially 
across much of south-central and eastern AZ by the middle of the 
week with rainfall amounts likely to be greater than 0.50-1.00", 
especially east of Phoenix. Minimum humidity levels in a 30-50% 
range will be common throughout the week with even higher readings
likely across eastern districts with good to excellent overnight 
recoveries. Temperatures will be in a near normal range during the
next couple of days before falling into a below normal category 
by the latter half of the week. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Lojero
LONG TERM...Lojero
AVIATION...Ryan 
FIRE WEATHER...Lojero
